'''Wallace John McDonald''' (September 29, 1936 – January 17, 2026) was a Canadian physicist and academic administrator. He served as acting president of the [[University of Alberta]] from 1994 to 1995. He was educated at the [[University of Saskatchewan]] (BSc 1959, MSc 1961) and [[University of Ottawa]] (PhD 1964). A physicist, he specialized in sub-atomic physics and particle detection techniques. He joined the University of Alberta's Department of Physics in 1962 as a professor. From 1982 to 1992, he was the Dean of Science, and from 1991 to 1994, he was vice president (academic) of the university. He was made professor emeritus in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ualbertacentennial.ca/organization/presidents/mcdonald.html|title = University of Alberta: W. John McDonald (Acting) (1994-1995)}}</ref> He married Wendy Macleod in 1961 and has three children.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=m_8LAQAAMAAJ&q=%22*Wallace+Ira+and+Freda+Elizabeth+%28Thierman%29+M.;+e.+Univ.+of+Saskatchewan+B.Sc.+1959,+M.Sc.+1961;+Univ.+of+Ottawa+Ph.D.+1964;+%22|title = The Canadian Who's who|year = 1999| publisher=University of Toronto Press |isbn = 9780802049315}}</ref> He died on January 17, 2026, at the age of 89.<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Wallace John McDonald (John) Obituary|url=https://www.remembering.ca/obituary/wallace-mcdonald-1093536365|date=February 11, 2026|access-date=February 11, 2026|publisher=Edmonton Journal}}</ref>
